label: words repair
system:
You write the narration of a short vertical cutaway explainer video whose pictures are ALREADY planned and built: a 3D diorama where a thing is built step by step while one narrator talks. You get its beats in order. For each: its role in the story, what the viewer SEES on screen during it, the idea it carries, and its cue words (the animation fires on them). Write exactly one sentence per beat, in that order.
THE ONE RULE: each sentence says what is on screen in its beat, and nothing its beat does not show. Where the idea and the picture disagree, follow the picture.
Cue words: every cue word of a beat appears in its sentence exactly as written (the same spelling and form: not a plural, not another tense), where it reads naturally.
The account's formula (keep it):
HOOK      "If you [one naive physical action], you have a [thing]." (16 words or fewer)
CHAIN     "But [the visible consequence]." then "So you [add the part]." Every "But…" after the first names the part the fix before it added, or starts with "But now" (checked by code).
NAME      "This is a [real term]."
MYTH-BUST "And [the thing everyone knows] is not [what they think]." then what it really is.
FINISH    "Add [the finishing touches shown]." (they complete the thing itself: "Add rocks round the edge, lily pads and fish.") then "Congratulations, you have built a [thing]."
Facts: a number or a surprising claim only from the verified facts given, with their exact numbers. No other numbers.
Spoken forms (the narration is read aloud, then checked word by word): "cannot", never "can not"; no abbreviations: never "US", "U.S." or "USA" (write "American" or "America"), units in full ("square feet", "pounds", "gallons"); numbers as digits with a comma for thousands ("1,500"), years as 4 digits ("1952"), times as "3 AM" (never "a.m.").
Every fix solves the problem before it, and says how: it names the problem's own thing ("But dirt keeps falling in, so you add a filter that catches the dirt", never "so you add a pump").
A checked fact is said as it was checked: a range stays a range ("every 8 to 10 hours", never "once every 8 hours").
Say what is true about the thing, never what the picture or a prop does: no "a glowing outline traces it", no "as the page says".
Plain words, present tense, American English, sentences of 6-20 words, no questions, no lists of more than three, no "you might think". Each sentence ends with a full stop.
user:
Topic: car brakes
Length: 30 s: 95-120 words in all, one sentence per beat (12 sentences).
Word budget: aim for 108 words in all, about 9 words a sentence (the hook up to 16; the name line and congrats short, so the others may run a little longer). Count before you answer: over 120 words is too long.
Verified facts (the only numbers and claims you may use, word for word where you use them):
- Brake fluid carries your push from a small piston at the pedal to bigger pistons at the wheel, multiplying the force about four to five times
- Repeated hard stops from high speed can heat a brake disc past 500 degrees Celsius
- Vented discs have air channels between their two faces whose vanes pump cooling air

The beats, in order:
1. hook
   on screen: a wooden block slides down and presses on the spinning tyre. actions: brake show; brake spin; down show (on "press"); brake press (on "press")
   idea: pressing a block on a spinning tire is the simplest brake
   cue words: "press"
2. problem
   on screen: dark smoke pours off the tyre where the block rubs. actions: down hide (on "But"); rub start (on "grinds"); smoke start (on "grinds")
   idea: the rubber grinds against the block and smokes
   cue words: "But", "grinds", "smoke"
3. fix1
   on screen: the block lifts off, a steel disc appears on the hub and a red caliper squeezes it. actions: smoke stop (on "So"); rub stop (on "So"); brake pressBack (on "So"); brake disc (on "disc"); brake caliper (on "squeeze")
   idea: a steel disc on the hub is squeezed instead of the tire
   cue words: "So", "disc", "squeeze"
4. problem2
   on screen: the speed sign stays at 60 while the disc keeps spinning. actions: stand a show (on "But"); speed show (on "But"); auto_fx 1 start (on "spinning")
   idea: a hand is too weak to stop the spinning disc
   cue words: "But", "spinning"
5. fix2
   on screen: a pedal, a master cylinder and a pipe to the caliper appear, orange fluid runs down it. actions: brake pedal (on "pedal"); brake master (on "pedal"); brake pipe (on "pipe"); brake fluid (on "fluid"); auto_fx 1 stop
   idea: a pedal pushes fluid down a pipe, which multiplies the push four to five times
   cue words: "pedal", "pipe", "fluid"
   its fact: Brake fluid carries your push from a small piston at the pedal to bigger pistons at the wheel, multiplying the force about four to five times
6. name
   on screen: a glowing outline traces the caliper on the disc. actions: brake outline show
   idea: the disc and its caliper are a disc brake
   cue words: (none)
7. how
   on screen: the pedal swings down, the pads clamp and the speed counts down to zero. actions: brake outline hide; brake step (on "pedal"); push show (on "pedal"); brake clamp (on "pads"); speed count (on "pads"); brake spinBack (on "stops")
   idea: the pedal pushes, the pads clamp the disc and the wheel stops
   cue words: "pedal", "pads", "stops"
8. problem3
   on screen: the disc glows red hot. actions: push hide (on "But"); speed hide (on "But"); heat show (on "But"); brake spin (on "But"); brake glow (on "glows")
   idea: hard stops heat the disc until it glows
   cue words: "But", "glows"
9. fix3
   on screen: vents open in the disc, white air arrows blow through and the glow fades. actions: brake vents (on "vents"); air show (on "air"); brake glowBack (on "cools")
   idea: vents let air through the disc to cool it
   cue words: "vents", "air", "cools"
   its fact: Vented discs have air channels between their two faces whose vanes pump cooling air
10. fact
   on screen: the heat gauge climbs to 500 and turns red. actions: air hide; heat count (on "500")
   idea: repeated hard stops can push a disc past 500 degrees Celsius
   cue words: "500"
   its fact: Repeated hard stops from high speed can heat a brake disc past 500 degrees Celsius
11. finish
   on screen: a red brake light appears on a post and glows as the pedal is pressed. actions: heat hide (on "Add"); brake lamp (on "glows"); brake lit (on "glows"); brake spinBack (on "glows")
   idea: a brake light completes it
   cue words: "Add", "glows"
12. congrats
   on screen: the finished build, calm
   idea: the finished disc brake, calm
   cue words: (none)
